title: pg_scann v4 IVF-AQ+AH Access Method — final measured head-to-head (SIFT1M, in-Postgres)
dataset: SIFT1M — full 1,000,000 base vectors (sift_base.fvecs), 200 queries (sift_query.fvecs), official SIFT ground-truth (sift_groundtruth.ivecs, valid at full 1M)
hardware: DigitalOcean droplet, 8 vCPU / 16 GB, single-threaded scan (pg17, port 28817)
method: COPY 1M rows into one table; build BOTH indexes on the SAME data (M46 same-data A/B rigor): v4 = theodb_ivfflat WITH (lists=1000, pq_subspaces=32, aq_threshold=2000) → batched-AH IVF-AQ scan; v3 = theodb_ivfflat WITH (lists=1000) → exact f32 IVF scan. recall@10 vs official GT; QPS = best-of-3 over 200 sequential index-scan queries per probe level; enable_seqscan=off.

index_size.note: delta = m=32 → 16 bytes/code × 1M = the AQ codes; confirms v4 is a real v4 index, not a v3 fallback

build_s.note: v4 only +0.7% despite AVQ train+encode — the M82 AQ_TRAIN_SAMPLE=50k stride sampling made the 1M train tractable

findings: The v4 IVF-AQ+AH Access Method index is FUNCTIONALLY CORRECT: recall@10 is byte-identical to the exact-f32 IVF at every probe level — the AH candidate pruning + exact rerank is lossless at these settings.
The v4 IVF-AQ+AH index delivers ZERO measured QPS advantage over the v3 exact-f32 IVF index in the page-based AM (differences are within best-of-3 timing noise, both directions).
At recall 0.985 (probes=32) the v4 index measures 78.5 QPS — the SAME class as M33's pgvector f32 IVF (78 QPS @ 0.99), and ~24x below ScaNN (1920 QPS @ 0.99).

Root cause: the AH per-candidate compute savings measured in the M75 in-memory spike (~5-7x) are MASKED in the AM by the dominant costs — centroid probing and list f32 page I/O — exactly the 'system-level overheads' documented by arXiv:2603.23710 (SIGMOD 2026). The M75 spike's own caveat ('no pgrx page/WAL tax — M76+') is confirmed: the tax + I/O binding erase the gain.
root_cause_analysis: In the current v4 page layout the AQ codes are interleaved with the f32 vectors in the same per-list pages ([ids][f32][codes]). Reading the codes to score by AH therefore also pages in the f32 vectors, so the scan pays the full f32 I/O regardless. The AH LUT scoring only saves the exact-distance COMPUTE, which is not the bottleneck — the AM scan is I/O + centroid-probe bound, not compute bound.
future_lever_honest_seed: To realize the AH speedup in the AM, the codes must live in SEPARATE pages from the f32 vectors so the scan reads only the compact code pages for the full list, prunes to top-K, then random-reads f32 ONLY for the K survivors (the FastScan/ScaNN storage separation). This is a layout redesign beyond M82's benchmark+verdict scope — recorded as an honest next-discovery seed, not shipped.
north_star_verdict: M82 CONFIRMS and EXTENDS the M73 verdict (ADR-0035): permissive-PostgreSQL-extension vector QPS superiority over ScaNN/AlloyDB is paradigmatically unreachable. M82 adds the specific, measured finding that even the AH-quantized in-memory speedup (M75) does not survive the page-based AM's I/O/probe binding. Permitted positioning: 'recall parity + billion-scale memory + AI-native/HTAP/open'; NEVER 'faster than AlloyDB on vectors'.
caveats: Single-threaded scan; multi-client QPS not measured here (M72 covered the multi-client regime at 128d).
The null result is specific to the current interleaved [ids][f32][codes] layout; a code/f32 page separation is an untested future lever (seed above), not a measured claim.
